sentences.text:
The relief sought for in the present writ petition is to direct the first respondent the 1st respondent to consider the Arbitration Application of the Petitioner dated 19.01.2023, under Section 24(1)(a)
and 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, and pass an Award by enhancing the compensation in respect of the Impugned Award dated 14.12.2001 in Award No.7/ 2001, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis passed by the 4th respondent fixing the compensation of Rs.64,596 /-in respect of the lands of the Petitioner in Survey No.669/2 measuring Hec. 0.68.0 Ares (Acres 1.69 cents) classified as Dry Maanavarai Lands Type - II at panruti Village, B Block, Sriperumbudur Taluk, Kancheepuram Distrct, acquired for SIPCOT Industrial Complex, DATCIT Oragadam Scheme - Unit 3 and the basic compensation payable to the Petitioner may be fixed at Rs.25,61,61,547.20 P.(Rupees Twnety Five Crores Sixty- One Lakhs Sixty One Thousand Five Hundred and Forty-Seven Paise Twenty only) as per law within a time frame fixed by this Court.
2. It is not in dispute that the land belonging to the petitioner was acquired for public projects.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The acquisition proceedings commenced during the year 25.11.1999 and an award was passed as early as on 14.12.2001.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The grievances of the writ petitioner is that he had not received any notice as mandated under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Since the petitioner had not received notice, he was deprived of submitting his objections during the relevant point of time.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Thus, the compensation determined by the authorities was questioned by the petitioner at a later point of time which was not considered by the authorities and therefore, the petitioner is constrained to move the present writ petition. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56224331/
2 3.

entities.text: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner mainly contended that even as per the document filed by the respondents, the notice was communicated to one Mr.M.S.Kannan, however the name of the petitioner is N.Dandapani and therefore, his contention is that no notice was served on him is established.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 4. The learned Special Government pleader raised an objection by stating that the petitioner is entitled to receive compensation under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and under Section 18(2) of the Act, the time limit for seeking enhancement also lapsed and thus, the compensation determined by the authorities alone is to be disbursed in favour of the writ petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The learned Special Government Pleader further states that the petitioner had knowledge about the acquisition in the year 2006.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, there is a long delay in filing an application seeking enhancement of compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the writ petition is to be rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5. Admittedly, the compensation deposited by the authorities is yet to be disbursed to the writ petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Though, the land was acquired in the year 2001, the petitioner has not received the compensation for the past about 22 years.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: As per the respondents, the amount was deposited in the work deposit and the deposit became lapsed since the petitioner did not withdraw the deposited amount.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The Right to property is a constitutional right.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Such right can be infringed only by the authority of law.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: In the present case, the land belonging to the petitioner was acquired and an award was passed on 14.12.2001.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The petitioner states that he had not received any notice during the relevant point of time and even as per the document produced by the respondents, the cover was addressed to Mr.M.S.Kannan and the name of the writ petitioner is Mr.N.Dandapani.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thus, there is a reason to believe that the notice during the relevant point of time was not properly served to the petitioner and therefore, he was deprived of submitting an objection for the acquisition proceedings initiated in the year 1999.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Though, the petitioner was aware of the acquisition proceedings in the year 2006,
he was deprived of submitting an application seeking enhancement of compensation and the amount deposited was also not disbursed to the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 7.Considering the overall facts and circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the benefit of filing an application seeking enhancement of compensation need not be denied to the writ petitioner since the notice of acquisition proceedings was not properly served on the petitioner during the relevant point of time.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 8.Accordingly, the respondents are directed to settle the compensation determined by them along with the interest as admissible under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the petitioner is at liberty to submit an application seeking enhancement of compensation under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
sentences._hearing_file: N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The authorities are directed not to reject the application if any N.Dandapani vs The District Collector And District ... on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56224331/
3 submitted by the petitioner seeking enhancement of compensation on the ground of delay and such application is to be decided on merits and in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible.
9.

sentences.text: for R1 to R4  JUDGMENT (Delivered by the Hon'ble Chief Justice) Heard Mr.M.Ramamoorthi, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr.K.Karthik Jegannath, learned Government Advocate for the respondents.

sentences.text: 2. The appellant/writ petitioner approached this court by filing a writ petition bearing W.P.No.7208 of 2023, seeking directions against the first respondent to consider the Arbitration Application filed by the appellant/writ petitioner dated 19.01.2023 under the provisions of Sections 24(1)(a) and 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 [for brevity, the Act of 2013] and sought further directions to fix the basic compensation of Rs.25,61,61,547/- (Rupees Twenty Five Crores Sixty One Lakhs Sixty One Thousand Five Hundred and Forty Seven Only). https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.

sentences.text: The court directed the respondents to settle the compensation amount within a period of four weeks and further granted liberty to the appellant/writ petitioner to file an application for enhancement of the compensation under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 [in short, Act of 1894].

sentences.text: The court also directed the authorities not to reject the application seeking enhancement of compensation on the ground of delay and such application is to be decided on merits.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the appellant/writ petitioner submits that in fact, the appellant/writ petitioner ought to have been granted the liberty to move under the provisions of the Act of 2013 and not under the old Act of 1894.

opennyai_summary.18_August_2023__arguments:
4. The learned Special Government pleader raised an objection by stating that the petitioner is entitled to receive compensation under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and under Section 18(2) of the Act, the time limit for seeking enhancement also lapsed and thus, the compensation determined by the authorities alone is to be disbursed in favour of the writ petitioner.

opennyai_summary.18_August_2023__ANALYSIS:
Though, the land was acquired in the year 2001, the petitioner has not received the compensation for the past about 22 years.
As per the respondents, the amount was deposited in the work deposit and the deposit became lapsed since the petitioner did not withdraw the deposited amount.
The Right to property is a constitutional right.
Such right can be infringed only by the authority of law.
In the present case, the land belonging to the petitioner was acquired and an award was passed on 14.12.2001.
Thus, there is a reason to believe that the notice during the relevant point of time was not properly served to the petitioner and therefore, he was deprived of submitting an objection for the acquisition proceedings initiated in the year 1999.
Though, the petitioner was aware of the acquisition proceedings in the year 2006,
he was deprived of submitting an application seeking enhancement of compensation and the amount deposited was also not disbursed to the petitioner.
